newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude steady to firmer, awaits U.S. lead.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude steady to firmer, awaits U.S. lead.

text.p: North Sea crude was firmer early on Monday but talk was thin with traders waiting for New York to provide direction after a long weekend in the United States.
IPE August Brent gained eight cents to $18.14 a barrel by 1206 GMT, steadying after a 79-cent slide late last week, and intermonth cash spreads were steady, with Aug/Sept trading twice at -11 cents.

Benchmark Dated Brent perked up to talk at August Brent +5/+15 cents, pulling prompt CFDs in its wake. This week was pegged at August Brent flat/+5 cents, a couple of cents firmer than late Friday levels.

Traders said tight Brent supply -- most of the July programme already nominated loading dates is in the hands of a European major -- and demand from an oil company to fill a VLCC committed into the U.S. Gulf were combining to lift values.
A slight improvement in Rotterdam refining margins at the end of last week after nearly a month of losses was also helping North Sea sentiment in the short term, they said.

The absence of Iraqi barrels was providing background support as was news that the Wilhelmshaven refinery in northern Germany had resumed operations at a higher rate of 210,000 barrels per day after a slight delay.
Only one Brent was expected to be nominated July 22-24 loading dates on Monday, traders said.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was steady but the few remaining July cargoes were being discussed around Dated Brent -80/-70 cents a barrel cif Augusta, slightly weaker than the last reported deal, with many refineries having covered their commitments until early August.
West African markets were thin, with dealers waiting for the release of the Nigerian loading programme for August, expected some time later this week.
